info.text:
In August 2026, Saudi Arabia reported pumping 6.238 million barrels of oil a day against an OPEC+ target of 10.416 million, about 40% under its quota and its lowest output since 1990 by its own count (outside estimates used by OPEC put it at 7.276 million, about 30% short). This video explains what OPEC and OPEC+ really are, from the 1960 founding in Baghdad and the 1973 embargo to the 1986, 2014-16 and 2020 price wars and the UAE's exit in May 2026. You'll see how quotas are set, why spare capacity matters, how US shale changed the game, and why the price itself is set in Brent and WTI futures markets. Every figure is dated, because OPEC+ targets can change from one monthly meeting to the next.
